claim: SUV39 class of methyltransferase enzymes deposits histone H3 lysine 9 di- and trimethylation (H3K9me2/3), the hallmark of constitutive heterochromatin.
source: The SUV39 class of methyltransferase enzymes deposits histone H3 lysine 9 di- and trimethylation (H3K9me2/3), the hallmark of constitutive heterochromatin.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field supported by scientific consensus and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Clr4 is the sole H3K9me2/3 methyltransferase in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
source: Clr4 is the sole H3K9me2/3 methyltransferase in the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe
evidence: This is established knowledge about the S. pombe heterochromatin system.

claim: Ubiquitination of lysine 14 on histone H3 (H3K14ub) plays a key role in H3K9 methylation.
source: recent evidence suggests that ubiquitination of lysine 14 on histone H3 (H3K14ub) plays a key role in H3K9 methylation.
evidence: The claim references recent evidence, indicating it is supported by prior research.

claim: The H3K14ub substrate binds specifically and tightly to the catalytic domain of Clr4.
source: Our structure-function approach shows that the H3K14ub substrate binds specifically and tightly to the catalytic domain of Clr4
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data including ITC measurements showing Kd of 80 ± 6 nM.

claim: H3K14ub stimulates Clr4 enzyme by over 250-fold.
source: Our structure-function approach shows that the H3K14ub substrate binds specifically and tightly to the catalytic domain of Clr4, and thereby stimulates the enzyme by over 250-fold.
evidence: This is supported by enzyme kinetics data showing 250-fold increase in kcat/KM.

claim: Mutations that disrupt the Clr4-H3K14ub interaction mechanism lead to a loss of H3K9me2/3.
source: Mutations that disrupt this mechanism lead to a loss of H3K9me2/3
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data showing complete loss of H3K9me2/3 in GS253 and 3FA mutants.

claim: Mutations that disrupt the Clr4-H3K14ub interaction abolish heterochromatin silencing similar to clr4 deletion.
source: Mutations that disrupt this mechanism lead to a loss of H3K9me2/3 and abolish heterochromatin silencing similar to clr4 deletion.
evidence: This is supported by growth assays and RT-qPCR data showing silencing defects comparable to clr4Δ.

claim: The Clr4 SET domain harbors a conserved sensor for H3K14ub.
source: Comparison with mammalian SET domain proteins suggests that the Clr4 SET domain harbors a conserved sensor for H3K14ub
evidence: This is based on comparison with mammalian proteins and HDX-MS data identifying the UBR region.

claim: The H3K14ub sensor mediates licensing of heterochromatin formation.
source: Comparison with mammalian SET domain proteins suggests that the Clr4 SET domain harbors a conserved sensor for H3K14ub, which mediates licensing of heterochromatin formation.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional data showing that disruption of H3K14ub binding abolishes heterochromatin.

claim: Histone methylation plays a critical role in regulating and organizing genomes to maintain genome integrity and establish appropriate gene regulation programs.
source: Histone methylation plays a critical role in regulating and organizing genomes to maintain genome integrity and establish appropriate gene regulation programs (Greer and Shi, 2012; Janssen et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: H3K9me2/3 are highly conserved hallmarks of heterochromatin.
source: Histone H3 lysine 9 di- and trimethylation (H3K9me2/3) are highly conserved hallmarks of heterochromatin
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: H3K9me2/3 marks provide a platform for the recruitment of chromatin effector complexes.
source: Histone H3 lysine 9 di- and trimethylation (H3K9me2/3) are highly conserved hallmarks of heterochromatin, where they provide a platform for the recruitment of chromatin effector complexes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of H3K9me2/3.

claim: H3K9me2/3 marks are dysregulated in various cancers, neurological diseases and viral latency.
source: H3K9me2/3 marks are dysregulated in various cancers, in neurological diseases and viral latency, and are targeted for therapeutic approaches (Kaniskan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The SUV39 clade of the SET-domain family of protein lysine methyltransferases represents the enzyme class depositing H3K9me2/3.
source: The SUV39 clade of the SET-domain family of protein lysine methyltransferases represents the enzyme class depositing H3K9me2/3 (Dillon et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: SUV39 proteins share a SET domain as a catalytic core.
source: They share a SET domain as a catalytic core
evidence: This is established knowledge about SUV39 protein structure.

claim: The SET domain builds on a series of curved β-sheets that are sandwiched between distinct pre- and post-SET domains.
source: They share a SET domain as a catalytic core, which builds on a series of curved β-sheets that are sandwiched between distinct pre- and post-SET domains
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about SET domains.

claim: The pre- and post-SET domains provide structural elements based on zinc-finger motifs.
source: which builds on a series of curved β-sheets that are sandwiched between distinct pre- and post-SET domains, providing structural elements based on zinc-finger motifs.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about SET domains.

claim: SUV39 enzymatic activity facilitates the transfer of a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) to the ε-amino group of lysine 9 on histone H3 with high specificity.
source: The SUV39 enzymatic activity facilitates the transfer of a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) to the ε-amino group of lysine 9 on histone H3 with high specificity
evidence: This is established knowledge about the enzymatic mechanism of SUV39 proteins.

claim: SUV39 enzymatic activity converts the cofactor SAM to S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH).
source: The SUV39 enzymatic activity facilitates the transfer of a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) to the ε-amino group of lysine 9 on histone H3 with high specificity, thereby converting the cofactor to S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the enzymatic mechanism.

claim: The mechanisms regulating SUV39 proteins to specifically deposit H3K9me2/3 in heterochromatic regions are not well understood.
source: The mechanisms regulating SUV39 proteins to specifically deposit H3K9me2/3 in heterochromatic regions are not well understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe heterochromatin system is closely related to the metazoan systems.
source: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe heterochromatin system, closely related to the metazoan systems
evidence: This is established knowledge about the evolutionary relationship of heterochromatin systems.

claim: The S. pombe heterochromatin system serves as a paradigm for studying the role of SUV39 proteins in heterochromatin establishment and maintenance.
source: The fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe heterochromatin system, closely related to the metazoan systems, with its sole SUV39 protein Clr4, serves as a paradigm for studying the role of this enzyme class in heterochromatin establishment and maintenance.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of S. pombe as a model system.

claim: Ectopic tethering experiments with Clr4 have established that H3K9me2/3 can support stable epigenetic transmission of transcriptional states.
source: Ectopic tethering experiments with Clr4 have established that H3K9me2/3 can support stable epigenetic transmission of transcriptional states (Audergon et al., 2015; Ragunathan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Clr4 and its animal orthologs share a very similar domain architecture consisting of an N-terminal chromodomain and a C-terminal catalytic SET domain.
source: Clr4 has further served as a valuable tool to understand its animal orthologs, which share a very similar domain architecture consisting of an N-terminal chromodomain and a C-terminal catalytic SET domain (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by structural knowledge and Figure 1A showing the domain organization.

claim: The chromodomain binds the H3K9me2/3 mark.
source: The chromodomain binds the H3K9me2/3 mark and is critical for spreading the H3K9me2/3 mark across genomic domains (Melcher et al., 2000; Müller et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The chromodomain is critical for spreading the H3K9me2/3 mark across genomic domains.
source: The chromodomain binds the H3K9me2/3 mark and is critical for spreading the H3K9me2/3 mark across genomic domains (Melcher et al., 2000; Müller et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: An autoinhibitory loop in the post-SET domain regulates spreading of H3K9me2/3 by Clr4.
source: Recent evidence also suggests that an autoinhibitory loop in the post-SET domain regulates spreading of H3K9me2/3 by Clr4 (Iglesias et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Full-length Clr4 shows strong stimulation by H3K14ub.
source: Methyltransferase time course on H3K14ub versus unmodified H3 peptides shows strong stimulation of full-length Clr4 and the isolated KMT domain by H3K14ub.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The isolated KMT domain of Clr4 shows strong stimulation by H3K14ub.
source: Methyltransferase time course on H3K14ub versus unmodified H3 peptides shows strong stimulation of full-length Clr4 and the isolated KMT domain by H3K14ub.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: H3K14ub elicits a 40-50-fold boost in Clr4 activity at a substrate concentration of 20 μM.
source: Quantification of the stimulation by the different substrates further showed that H3K14ub elicits a 40–50-fold boost in activity at a substrate concentration of 20 μM (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: H3K18ub is a significantly poorer substrate than H3K14ub for Clr4.
source: H3K18ub is a significantly poorer substrate than H3K14ub, demonstrating that the position of the ubiquitin modification on the H3 tail is critical for optimal Clr4 stimulation
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing H3K14ub and H3K18ub activity.

claim: The position of the ubiquitin modification on the H3 tail is critical for optimal Clr4 stimulation.
source: H3K18ub is a significantly poorer substrate than H3K14ub, demonstrating that the position of the ubiquitin modification on the H3 tail is critical for optimal Clr4 stimulation
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of H3K14ub and H3K18ub activity data.

claim: Covalent linkage generating high local ubiquitin concentration is not sufficient for Clr4 stimulation.
source: demonstrating that the position of the ubiquitin modification on the H3 tail is critical for optimal Clr4 stimulation and that covalent linkage generating high local ubiquitin concentration is not sufficient.
evidence: This is inferred from the H3K18ub data showing poor stimulation despite covalent linkage.

claim: The KMT domain is sufficient to mediate the H3K14ub regulatory mechanism.
source: However, in contrast to the previous study, we observe that the KMT domain is sufficient to mediate this regulatory mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that the isolated KMT domain is stimulated by H3K14ub.

claim: The Michaelis-Menten constant (KM) for Clr4KMT on H3K14ub is 0.33 ± 0.06 µM.
source: An approximately hundred-fold difference for the Michaelis–Menten (KM) constants was measured with 0.33 ± 0.06 µM for H3K14ub
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from enzyme kinetics.

claim: The Michaelis-Menten constant (KM) for Clr4KMT on unmodified H3 is 28.1 ± 8.0 µM.
source: An approximately hundred-fold difference for the Michaelis–Menten (KM) constants was measured with 0.33 ± 0.06 µM for H3K14ub and 28.1 ± 8.0 µM for H3.
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from enzyme kinetics.

claim: There is an approximately hundred-fold difference in KM between H3K14ub and unmodified H3 for Clr4KMT.
source: An approximately hundred-fold difference for the Michaelis–Menten (KM) constants was measured with 0.33 ± 0.06 µM for H3K14ub and 28.1 ± 8.0 µM for H3.
evidence: This is calculated from the measured KM values.

claim: The turnover number (kcat) for Clr4KMT on H3K14ub is 0.81 ± 0.03 min⁻¹.
source: The turnover number (kcat) was about three times higher in the presence of H3K14ub (0.81 ± 0.03 min–1)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from enzyme kinetics.

claim: The turnover number (kcat) for Clr4KMT on unmodified H3 is 0.28 ± 0.02 min⁻¹.
source: The turnover number (kcat) was about three times higher in the presence of H3K14ub (0.81 ± 0.03 min–1) compared with unmodified H3 (0.28 ± 0.02 min–1).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from enzyme kinetics.

claim: The kcat is about three times higher in the presence of H3K14ub compared with unmodified H3.
source: The turnover number (kcat) was about three times higher in the presence of H3K14ub (0.81 ± 0.03 min–1) compared with unmodified H3 (0.28 ± 0.02 min–1).
evidence: This is calculated from the measured kcat values.

claim: H3K14ub leads to a 250-fold increase in overall enzymatic efficiency (kcat/KM) of Clr4KMT.
source: This leads to an increase in overall enzymatic efficiency measured by the specificity constant ksp = kcat/KM of 250-fold (Table 1).
evidence: This is calculated from the measured kinetic parameters shown in Table 1.

claim: The presence of ubiquitin on lysine 14 leads to a tighter enzyme-substrate complex.
source: Comparison of the kinetic parameters between H3K14ub and H3 substrate indicates that the presence of ubiquitin on lysine 14 leads to a tighter enzyme-substrate complex
evidence: This is inferred from the 100-fold lower KM for H3K14ub.

claim: The presence of ubiquitin on lysine 14 leads to conformational changes in the active site that increase the rate of the methyltransferase reaction.
source: Comparison of the kinetic parameters between H3K14ub and H3 substrate indicates that the presence of ubiquitin on lysine 14 leads to a tighter enzyme-substrate complex and to conformational changes in the active site that increase the rate of the methyltransferase reaction.
evidence: This is inferred from the 3-fold increase in kcat for H3K14ub.

claim: Free ubiquitin does not significantly increase Clr4 activity on unmodified H3.
source: While we observed no significant increase in activity for unmodified H3, we observed a drop in the activity for H3K14ub at high concentrations of free ubiquitin (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: High concentrations of free ubiquitin cause a drop in Clr4 activity on H3K14ub.
source: While we observed no significant increase in activity for unmodified H3, we observed a drop in the activity for H3K14ub at high concentrations of free ubiquitin (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The ubiquitin competition experiment failed to produce evidence of an allosteric site for free ubiquitin on Clr4.
source: This experiment failed to produce evidence of an allosteric site for free ubiquitin on Clr4
evidence: This is concluded from the ubiquitin competition assay results.

claim: The stimulation of kcat likely depends on an induced-fit mechanism triggered by binding of H3K14ub to the Clr4KMT domain.
source: we conclude that the stimulation of kcat is likely to depend on an induced-fit mechanism triggered by binding of H3K14ub to the Clr4KMT domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of allosteric effects and the kinetic data.

claim: HDX-MS analysis showed a strong and unique reduction of the HDX rate for residues 243-261 of Clr4 in the presence of H3K14ub.
source: Comparing the dynamics for Clr4KMT alone and in the presence of excess H3K14ub or unmodified H3 peptides, we observed a strong and unique reduction of the HDX rate for residues 243–261 of Clr4 in the presence of H3K14ub (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary files 2-4).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from HDX-MS shown in Figure 2.

claim: Residues 291-305 of Clr4 showed significant amide protection by both H3 and H3K14ub substrates.
source: A further region between residues 291–305 showed significant amide protection by both H3 and H3K14ub substrates, the latter peptide showing a more intense protection (Figure 2B, bottom graph).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from HDX-MS shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The H3 peptide interacts with residues 291-305 of Clr4.
source: These results suggest that the H3 peptide interacts with residues 291–305
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing protection of this region by H3 peptides.

claim: The ubiquitin moiety binds to a region involving residues 243-261 of Clr4.
source: These results suggest that the H3 peptide interacts with residues 291–305, while the ubiquitin moiety binds to a region involving residues 243–261.
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing specific protection of this region by H3K14ub.

claim: The H3K14ub binding region identified by HDX-MS maps to the NT domain just before it transitions into the pre-SET domain.
source: The H3K14ub binding region identified by HDX-MS maps to the NT domain just before it transitions into the pre-SET domain, and we will refer to this region as UBR (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on mapping the HDX-MS data onto the known Clr4 structure.

claim: The UBR forms a ridge along the 'back' of Clr4, opposite to the active site pockets.
source: The UBR forms a ridge along the 'back' of Clr4, opposite to the active site pockets where cofactor and the substrate peptide bind (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Amino acids 25-43 on ubiquitin were protected from HDX upon interaction with Clr4.
source: We also compared HDX-MS rates of isolated H3K14ub peptide with the H3K14ub-Clr4 complex and found that amino acids 25–43 on ubiquitin were protected from exchange upon interaction with Clr4 (Figure 2D and E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from HDX-MS shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Residues 25-43 of ubiquitin map to the α-helix of ubiquitin.
source: These residues map to the α-helix of ubiquitin, indicating that this surface interacts with Clr4.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of ubiquitin structure.

claim: The α-helix surface of ubiquitin interacts with Clr4.
source: These residues map to the α-helix of ubiquitin, indicating that this surface interacts with Clr4.
evidence: This is inferred from the HDX-MS data showing protection of the α-helix region.

claim: Clr4-GS253 mutant resulted in a stable protein.
source: While substitutions of residues 243–251 yielded unstable protein, substitution of residues 253–256 (sequence DPNF to GGSG, referred to as Clr4-GS253) resulted in a stable protein.
evidence: This is based on experimental observation during protein purification.

claim: Substitutions of residues 243-251 in Clr4 yielded unstable protein.
source: While substitutions of residues 243–251 yielded unstable protein
evidence: This is based on experimental observation during protein purification.

claim: Clr4 binds to the H3K14ub peptide with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 80 ± 6 nM.
source: Consistent with the low KM observed previously, Clr4 binds to the H3K14ub peptide with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 80 ± 6 nM in a reaction that is dominated by enthalpy (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from ITC shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Clr4-H3K14ub binding reaction is dominated by enthalpy.
source: Consistent with the low KM observed previously, Clr4 binds to the H3K14ub peptide with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 80 ± 6 nM in a reaction that is dominated by enthalpy (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from ITC shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Clr4-GS253 showed complete loss of binding to H3K14ub.
source: In contrast, Clr4-GS253 and Clr4-3FA showed complete loss of binding to H3K14ub under the same conditions (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from ITC shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Clr4-3FA showed complete loss of binding to H3K14ub.
source: In contrast, Clr4-GS253 and Clr4-3FA showed complete loss of binding to H3K14ub under the same conditions (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from ITC shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: The UBR mutants disrupt the Clr4-H3K14ub enzyme-substrate complex.
source: The ITC data confirm that H3K14ub binds with high affinity to the KMT domain of Clr4 and that the UBR mutants disrupt the Clr4-H3K14ub enzyme-substrate complex.
evidence: This is concluded from the ITC data showing loss of binding for the mutants.

claim: The Clr4-3FA crystal structure was solved at 2.46 Å resolution.
source: These efforts resulted in a 2.46 Å structure of Clr4-3FA (Table 2).
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data from X-ray crystallography.

claim: No significant difference in global or local protein folding was observed between wild-type Clr4 KMT domains and the Clr4-3FA mutant.
source: When comparing with previous X-ray structures of Clr4, we observed no significant difference in global or local protein folding between the wild-type Clr4 KMT domains and the Clr4-3FA mutant (RMSD = 0.37 Å) (Figure 3D and E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison with RMSD calculation.

claim: The Clr4-3FA mutations do not induce significant structural changes.
source: This indicates that the Clr4-3FA mutations do not induce significant structural changes.
evidence: This is concluded from the structural comparison showing low RMSD.

claim: The UBR mutants lose activity on H3K14ub when compared to wild-type Clr4KMT.
source: These assays show that the mutants lose activity on H3K14ub when compared to wild-type Clr4KMT (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The efficiency of Clr4-3FA on H3K14ub drops approximately 27-fold compared to wild-type.
source: Comparison of the specificity constants ksp shows that the efficiency of the UBR mutants on H3K14ub drops approximately 27-fold for Clr4-3FA and 48-fold for Clr4-GS253 compared to the wild-type.
evidence: This is calculated from the measured kinetic parameters in Table 1.

claim: The efficiency of Clr4-GS253 on H3K14ub drops approximately 48-fold compared to wild-type.
source: Comparison of the specificity constants ksp shows that the efficiency of the UBR mutants on H3K14ub drops approximately 27-fold for Clr4-3FA and 48-fold for Clr4-GS253 compared to the wild-type.
evidence: This is calculated from the measured kinetic parameters in Table 1.

claim: The drop in activity of UBR mutants on H3K14ub is caused by a corresponding drop in KM.
source: This drop in activity is caused by a corresponding drop in KM, consistent with the ITC results.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the kinetic parameters in Table 1.

claim: The activity of Clr4-3FA on unmodified H3 peptides is 91% of wild-type.
source: In contrast to the enzymatic activity on H3K14ub, the activity on unmodified H3 peptides is only mildly affected resulting in a ksp, that is, 91% of wild-type for Clr4-3FA
evidence: This is calculated from the measured kinetic parameters in Table 1.

claim: The activity of Clr4-GS253 on unmodified H3 peptides is 78% of wild-type.
source: In contrast to the enzymatic activity on H3K14ub, the activity on unmodified H3 peptides is only mildly affected resulting in a ksp, that is, 91% of wild-type for Clr4-3FA and 78% for Clr4-GS253 (Figure 3G, Table 1).
evidence: This is calculated from the measured kinetic parameters in Table 1.

claim: Both UBR mutants target the Clr4-H3K14ub interaction with high specificity.
source: We conclude that the enzymatic and affinity measurements establish that both UBR mutants target the Clr4-H3K14ub interaction with high specificity.
evidence: This is concluded from the differential effects on H3K14ub versus unmodified H3.

claim: Heterochromatin formation in S. pombe depends strongly on the H3K9me2/3 methyltransferase activity of Clr4.
source: In S. pombe, heterochromatin formation depends strongly on the H3K9me2/3 methyltransferase activity of Clr4.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the S. pombe heterochromatin system.

claim: Clr4 knock-out strains are defective for transcriptional gene silencing.
source: Clr4 knock-out and mutant strains are defective for transcriptional gene silencing and display hyperacetylated heterochromatic regions (Nakayama et al., 2001; Bannister et al., 2001; Gerace et al., 2010; Iglesias et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Clr4 knock-out strains display hyperacetylated heterochromatic regions.
source: Clr4 knock-out and mutant strains are defective for transcriptional gene silencing and display hyperacetylated heterochromatic regions (Nakayama et al., 2001; Bannister et al., 2001; Gerace et al., 2010; Iglesias et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The clr4-GS253 mutant showed increased growth on medium lacking uracil.
source: The clr4-GS253 mutant showed increased growth on medium lacking uracil, no growth on FOA plates, and white colonies on low adenine, comparable to the clr4Δ mutant, which indicates a severe loss of transcriptional gene silencing (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The clr4-GS253 mutant showed no growth on FOA plates.
source: The clr4-GS253 mutant showed increased growth on medium lacking uracil, no growth on FOA plates, and white colonies on low adenine, comparable to the clr4Δ mutant, which indicates a severe loss of transcriptional gene silencing (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The clr4-GS253 mutant showed white colonies on low adenine medium.
source: The clr4-GS253 mutant showed increased growth on medium lacking uracil, no growth on FOA plates, and white colonies on low adenine, comparable to the clr4Δ mutant, which indicates a severe loss of transcriptional gene silencing (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The clr4-GS253 mutant phenotype indicates a severe loss of transcriptional gene silencing.
source: The clr4-GS253 mutant showed increased growth on medium lacking uracil, no growth on FOA plates, and white colonies on low adenine, comparable to the clr4Δ mutant, which indicates a severe loss of transcriptional gene silencing (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is inferred from the growth assay results being comparable to clr4Δ.

claim: The clr4-3FA mutant showed a growth phenotype very similar to clr4Δ.
source: The clr4-3FA mutant also showed a growth phenotype very similar to clr4Δ.
evidence: This is directly observed experimental data from growth assays.

claim: The silencing defect in clr4-3FA is less severe than in clr4-GS253 or clr4Δ.
source: However, the slightly pinkish color on low Ade plates suggests that the silencing defect is less severe than in clr4-GS253 or clr4Δ.
evidence: This is inferred from the colony color phenotype.

claim: The clr4 mutants are expressed at normal levels.
source: The clr4 mutants are expressed at normal levels, and co-IP experiments with Rik1 show that they remain associated with the CLRC complex (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The clr4 mutants remain associated with the CLRC complex.
source: The clr4 mutants are expressed at normal levels, and co-IP experiments with Rik1 show that they remain associated with the CLRC complex (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is supported by co-IP data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Transcript levels of centromeric dg/dh repeats and telomeric tlh1 locus were greatly elevated in the clr4-GS253 mutant, similar to clr4Δ.
source: The levels of these transcripts were greatly elevated in the clr4-GS253 mutant, similar to clr4Δ.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The 3FA mutant showed high transcript levels for centromeric dh and telomeric transcripts.
source: In contrast, the 3FA mutant showed a more nuanced silencing defect with high transcript levels for centromeric dh and telomeric transcripts, and a modest ~10-fold increase for centromeric dg.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The 3FA mutant showed a modest ~10-fold increase in centromeric dg transcripts.
source: In contrast, the 3FA mutant showed a more nuanced silencing defect with high transcript levels for centromeric dh and telomeric transcripts, and a modest ~10-fold increase for centromeric dg.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Both H3K9me2 and H3K9me3 were completely abolished in clr4-GS253 and clr4-3FA strains at centromeric dg/dh repeats.
source: Both H3K9me2 and H3K9me3 were completely abolished in clr4-GS253 and clr4-3FA strains at centromeric dg/dh repeats, being indistinguishable from clr4Δ.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: clr4-GS253 showed elevated levels of H3K9me1 when compared to wild-type clr4+.
source: clr4-GS253 and clr4Δ also showed elevated levels of H3K9me1 when compared to wild-type clr4+, while this was not observed for clr4-3FA.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: clr4Δ showed elevated levels of H3K9me1 when compared to wild-type clr4+.
source: clr4-GS253 and clr4Δ also showed elevated levels of H3K9me1 when compared to wild-type clr4+, while this was not observed for clr4-3FA.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Elevated H3K9me1 marks support the hypothesis that another unidentified methyltransferase could be depositing this mark.
source: The elevated H3K9me1 marks support the hypothesis that another unidentified methyltransferase could be depositing this mark (Jih et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by the data and a citation.

claim: RNA polymerase II occupancy at dh repeats was strongly increased in clr4 mutants.
source: We further found that in agreement with the increased transcript levels RNA polymerase II occupancy at dh repeats was strongly increased.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The severity of the UBR mutant phenotype correlates with the degree of loss of enzymatic function on H3K14ub in vitro.
source: Furthermore, the severity of the phenotype correlates with the degree of loss of enzymatic function on H3K14ub in vitro, consistent with Clr4's KMT domain mediating the crosstalk between H3K14ub and H3K9me2/3 as an essential step in heterochromatin formation and maintenance.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the in vitro and in vivo data for the mutants.

claim: Clr4's KMT domain mediates the crosstalk between H3K14ub and H3K9me2/3 as an essential step in heterochromatin formation and maintenance.
source: Furthermore, the severity of the phenotype correlates with the degree of loss of enzymatic function on H3K14ub in vitro, consistent with Clr4's KMT domain mediating the crosstalk between H3K14ub and H3K9me2/3 as an essential step in heterochromatin formation and maintenance.
evidence: This is concluded from the correlation between in vitro and in vivo phenotypes.

claim: SUV39H2 consistently showed stimulation by H3K14ub.
source: Of our candidate enzymes, SUV39H2, consistently showed stimulation by H3K14ub, while we could not detect stimulation for G9a or SUVH4.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: G9a did not show stimulation by H3K14ub.
source: Of our candidate enzymes, SUV39H2, consistently showed stimulation by H3K14ub, while we could not detect stimulation for G9a or SUVH4.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SUVH4 did not show stimulation by H3K14ub.
source: Of our candidate enzymes, SUV39H2, consistently showed stimulation by H3K14ub, while we could not detect stimulation for G9a or SUVH4.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The H3K14ub-mediated stimulation is conserved in a subset of SUV39 family proteins in higher eukaryotes.
source: These results suggest that the H3K14ub-mediated stimulation is conserved in a subset of SUV39 family proteins in higher eukaryotes
evidence: This is inferred from the SUV39H2 stimulation data.

claim: H3K14ub is potentially implicated in the regulation of H3K9 methylation in mammalian heterochromatin.
source: These results suggest that the H3K14ub-mediated stimulation is conserved in a subset of SUV39 family proteins in higher eukaryotes, and that H3K14ub is potentially implicated in the regulation of H3K9 methylation in mammalian heterochromatin.
evidence: This is speculated based on the SUV39H2 data.

claim: H3K14ub serves as a licensing mechanism for the deposition of H3K9me2/3 marks and heterochromatin formation.
source: Based on these and our findings, we propose that H3K14ub serves as a licensing mechanism for the deposition of H3K9me2/3 marks and heterochromatin formation (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claim: Acetylation of H3K14 serves to prevent ubiquitination of H3K14 similar to a protecting group in organic chemical synthesis.
source: In this model, acetylation of H3K14, which is strongly associated with euchromatin, assumes a much more specific role than normally associated with histone acetylation: it serves to prevent ubiquitination of H3K14 similar to a protecting group in organic chemical synthesis.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model proposed based on the findings.

claim: The H3K14ac-specific HDACs Clr3 and Sir2 indirectly control H3K9me2/3 by regulating the availability of H3K14 for ubiquitination by the CLRC ubiquitin ligase complex.
source: The H3K14ac-specific HDACs Clr3 and Sir2 therefore indirectly control H3K9me2/3 by regulating the availability of H3K14 for ubiquitination by the CLRC ubiquitin ligase complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the proposed licensing model.

claim: Mutations of H3K14 lead to loss of H3K9 methylation.
source: Consistent with this model, mutations of H3K14 lead to loss of H3K9 methylation (Mellone et al., 2003)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Double deletion of Clr3 and Sir2 phenocopies mutations of H3K14.
source: Consistent with this model, mutations of H3K14 lead to loss of H3K9 methylation (Mellone et al., 2003), which is phenocopied by double deletion of Clr3 and Sir2 (Alper et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Ubiquitination is essential for the establishment of heterochromatin.
source: The genetic data further suggests that ubiquitination is essential for the establishment of heterochromatin since mutants of the CLRC complex are completely devoid of heterochromatin (Horn et al., 2005; Jia et al., 2005; Li et al., 2005; Nakayama et al., 2001; Thon et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Mutants of the CLRC complex are completely devoid of heterochromatin.
source: The genetic data further suggests that ubiquitination is essential for the establishment of heterochromatin since mutants of the CLRC complex are completely devoid of heterochromatin (Horn et al., 2005; Jia et al., 2005; Li et al., 2005; Nakayama et al., 2001; Thon et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Recognition of H3K14ub by Clr4 is critically important for the establishment and maintenance of heterochromatin.
source: In the clr4-GS253 and clr4-3FA mutants, we observe a severe loss of heterochromatin, which validates that recognition of H3K14ub by Clr4 is critically important for the establishment and maintenance of heterochromatin.
evidence: This is concluded from the severe heterochromatin defects in the UBR mutants.

claim: H3K14ub and the Clr4 UBR are critical factors for sequestration of Clr4 on H3K9M mutants.
source: In a parallel study, Shan et al. have shown that H3K14ub and the Clr4 UBR are critical factors for sequestration of Clr4 on H3K9M mutants, which mimic oncogenic histone lysine-to-methionine mutants (Shan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a parallel study.

claim: The HDX-MS and mutagenesis results provide constraints for predicting the atomic structure of the Clr4-H3K14ub complex.
source: The HDX-MS and mutagenesis results provide a valuable set of constraints that we employed to predict the atomic structure of the Clr4-H3K14ub complex by protein-protein docking using HADDOCK (Dominguez et al., 2003).
evidence: This describes the computational approach used to generate the structural model.

claim: The Clr4-H3K14ub model shows that the H3K14ub peptide can fit the H3 peptide into the binding groove and simultaneously cover Clr4 residues 253-256 and F427 with its K14-linked ubiquitin moiety.
source: The resulting model (Figure 5C) shows that the H3K14ub peptide can comfortably fit the H3 peptide into the binding groove and simultaneously cover Clr4 residues 253–256 mutated in Clr4-GS253 and F427 mutated in Clr4-3FA with its K14-linked ubiquitin moiety.
evidence: This describes the structural model shown in Figure 5C.

claim: F310 is unlikely to be involved directly in the interaction with ubiquitin.
source: The model suggests that F310, which is also mutated in Clr4-3FA, is unlikely to be involved directly in the interaction with ubiquitin as the N-terminal residues 253–256 shield F310 from interacting with ubiquitin (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural model shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The UBR corresponds structurally to the 'SET activation loop' (SAL) observed in PRC2 structures.
source: Intriguingly, the UBR that we identified by HDX-MS corresponds structurally to the 'SET activation loop' (SAL) observed in PRC2 structures, which stabilizes the SET-I domain, a region inside the SET domain that provides one side of the peptide binding groove (Qian and Zhou, 2006; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison with PRC2 and citations.

claim: The SAL in PRC2 stabilizes the SET-I domain.
source: Intriguingly, the UBR that we identified by HDX-MS corresponds structurally to the 'SET activation loop' (SAL) observed in PRC2 structures, which stabilizes the SET-I domain, a region inside the SET domain that provides one side of the peptide binding groove (Qian and Zhou, 2006; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on PRC2 structure.

claim: The SET-I domain provides one side of the peptide binding groove.
source: Intriguingly, the UBR that we identified by HDX-MS corresponds structurally to the 'SET activation loop' (SAL) observed in PRC2 structures, which stabilizes the SET-I domain, a region inside the SET domain that provides one side of the peptide binding groove (Qian and Zhou, 2006; Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about SET domains.

claim: In MLL complexes, RBBP5 assumes a similar position as the SAL in PRC2 and stabilizes the SET-I domain in coordination with ASH2L.
source: In a further example, the mixed lineage leukemia complexes with catalytic SET domain proteins MLL1 or MLL3 are activated by structural rearrangement of the regulatory subunits RBBP5 and ASH2L. RBBP5 thereby assumes a similar position as the SAL in PRC2 and stabilizes the SET-I domain in coordination with ASH2L (Li et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature on MLL complexes.

claim: Complex formation of MLL3 with ASH2L-RBBP5 significantly reduced the conformational dynamics of the SET-I domain.
source: In these experiments, apo MLL3 and the MLL3-ASH2L-RBBP5 complex showed little structural differences in the positioning of SET-I, but complex formation significantly reduced the conformational dynamics of the SET-I domain.
evidence: This is based on prior experimental observations.

claim: The SET-I domain is a potential mediator of the H3K14ub stimulation.
source: The structural similarities between these regulatory mechanisms identify the SET-I domain as a potential mediator of the H3K14ub stimulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural similarities with other SET domain regulatory mechanisms.

claim: In the Clr4-H3K14ub model, the SET-I domain is sandwiched between the H3K14-linked ubiquitin moiety and the H3 peptide bound in the active site.
source: In our model, the SET-I domain is sandwiched between the H3K14-linked ubiquitin moiety and the H3 peptide bound in the active site (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This describes the structural model shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Binding of H3K14ub to Clr4 might contribute to high substrate affinity and an optimally organized active site.
source: Therefore, binding of H3K14ub to Clr4 might not only contribute to high substrate affinity but also to an optimally organized active site.
evidence: This is speculated based on the structural model and kinetic data.

claim: The UBR sequence is well conserved in the Ascomycetes clade of fungi.
source: Bioinformatic analysis of the UBR sequence using Hidden Markov Models suggests that the UBR sequence is well conserved in the Ascomycetes clade of fungi, which includes the Neurospora crassa Dim-5 protein for example (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: SUV39H2's UBR motif is similar to Clr4, while G9a and SUVH4 diverge significantly.
source: Comparing the Clr4 motif with motifs obtained using homologous sequences from human SUV39H2, human G9a, and Arabidopsis SUVH4 shows that SUV39H2's motif is similar to Clr4, while G9a and SUVH4 diverge significantly.
evidence: This is based on sequence comparison analysis.

claim: The similarity of SUV39H2's UBR motif to Clr4 is consistent with H3K14ub stimulating SUV39H2 but not G9A or SUVH4.
source: This is consistent with our observation that H3K14ub can stimulate SUV39H2, but not G9A or SUVH4.
evidence: This connects the sequence conservation with the functional data.

claim: H3K14ub has been detected in human cells by mass spectrometry.
source: The function of H3K14ub in human cells is poorly understood, but it has been detected by mass spectrometry (Harrison et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The crosstalk observed in fission yeast between H3K14ub and H3K9me2/3 is conserved in mammals.
source: In combination with the conservation of the H3K14ub mediated stimulation in SUV39H2, this suggests that the crosstalk observed in fission yeast is conserved in mammals.
evidence: This is inferred from the SUV39H2 stimulation data and sequence conservation.
